newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy poised to rejoin ERM in EMU drive.
newsitem.headline: Italy poised to rejoin ERM in EMU drive.

text.p: Italy was poised to rejoin Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at the weekend, as European union members scramble to qualify for the single currency due to be launched in January 1999.

An Italian news agency quoted Prime Minister Romano Prodi as saying that the lira would return to the currency grid in a matter of "a few hours or a few days", as approval of the country's budget had allowed technical talks to begin.

"We are exchanging the necessary data for a lira return to the ERM," the AGI agency quoted Prodi as saying after weeks of speculation about his country's ability to press ahead with its cherished aim of being at the launch of the single currency.

The report came as German Chancellor Helmut Kohl raised hopes that more countries than recently anticipated may join the single currency from day one and France, which has seen its own franc under pressure this week on EMU-related fears, pledged support for lira entry if the terms are right.
A senior source at a European Banking Congress in Frankfurt told Reuters Italy had asked for a key European Union monetary policy body to meet on Saturday.

"The Italians have requested a meeting of the monetary committee for tomorrow," the source said. There was no official confirmation of the meeting, which would agree the exchange parity between the lira and other currencies in the ERM.

But Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi suggested earlier that differences had receded between Italy and its main European Union partners over the touchy issue of what level was appropriate for the lira's return to the ERM.

There was "no evidence" that France or Germany were seeking to delay the timing of the currency's reentry, he told reporters at the banking conference, which drew many top finance and monetary officials from throughout Europe.
"Italy intends to be one of the founding members of the EMU", he said. "Italians are determined to do everything necessary to be an element of stability and not an element of tension or distortion".
A stable two year-stint within the ERM currency grid is one of the criteria for countries wishing to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Germany's Kohl, a driving force behind European integration, fanned hopes the planned currency union would be wider than many expect by saying as many fully-qualified countries should join as possible.
"The goal must be that as many nations meet the stability criteria and participate in the currency union from the beginning," he told the conference.

European countries which want to include their currencies in the planned Euro from 1999 are rushing to meet economic targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budget deficits and public debt in the 1997 year - necessary if they are to be at the launch.

Most are facing the greatest problems in meeting the fiscal targets, which call for budget deficits to run at a maximum of three percent of gross domestic product and public debt at a maximum of 60 percent of GDP.
The French franc fell this week on mounting jitters over the merits of the government's "strong franc" policy and concerns over relentless belt-tightening to meet the tough EMU criteria.

French President Jacques Chirac flew home on Friday from a state visit to Japan to find his country in political turmoil, with angry truck drivers blockading highways and fuel depots to demand pay rises, shorter hours and early retirement.
But the france recovered from Thursday's low of 3.3975 per mark, and economists said a switch in attention to the lira this weekend could remove some of the pressure.

The Italian government does not want the lira to re-enter the grid at too high a level because of the adverse effect on its exports, but the French want it in at a less competitive rate because of the impact on their own industry.

In Helsinki, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said he expected the European Union summit next month in Dublin to agree on a controversial budget stability pact for EMU. Even if it was delayed, monetary union would not be derailed, he said.
"If we don't reach it in Dublin, that's not the end of the day. It can be reached in January or February," Bruton said.
Germany wants a strict definition of the economic circumstances which would exempt an EMU member from paying a stiff penalty if it slips up on the deficit criteria.
But the country is also facing problems triggered by EMU belt-tightening. Up to 40,000 German bank workers staged nationwide protests on Friday against cuts by employers to sick pay entitlements.
